briefs.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 large, well-known US companies, like Apple, Walmart and Coca-Cola. It is one of the oldest stock market measures, started in 1896.
briefs.whyMoved: The Dow fell 1.11%, or 561.25 points, on Wednesday to 50,198.17, its fifth loss in a row and the worst of the big indexes; it was 53,356.12 on November 4, so it has lost about 5.9% in two weeks. Dow member UnitedHealth fell about 6% after the government proposed a new plan to fight fraud in health programs, and fellow insurers Humana and CVS fell too. Nvidia, another Dow member, slid 2.9%. Because the Dow holds only 30 companies, one big drop pulls the whole average much harder; health insurers earn much of their money from government health plans, so new rules on those payments can shrink their profits.

watch.what: Walmart earnings: strong sales would show shoppers are fine and help the Dow; weak sales would add to the slide.
Fed decision: a quarter-point hike is expected; a half-point hike would be a bigger hit.

briefs.name: Russell 2000
briefs.headline: Russell 2000 edges up 0.46% as rates and oil slip
briefs.summary: The Fed held its key rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but two officials, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted to raise it. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years. Target, Lowe's and TJX all reported results that beat or pleased investors on Wednesday.
bull: The 10-year rate eased to about 5.07%, a small break on borrowing costs, which matter more for small companies.
US oil fell 3.04% to $82.08, lowering fuel costs for small businesses like truckers and restaurants.
Target and Lowe's beat forecasts, and small companies earn most of their money inside the US, so steady shoppers help them.
bear: Fed official Christopher Waller said a half-point hike may be needed in December, and rate traders already fully expect at least a quarter-point hike.
Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October to the lowest since at least 2001, bad for small builders and home-related firms.
Waller said inflation is 'headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out', which could mean more hikes after December.
briefs.nextEvent: Fed interest rate decision on Wednesday, December 9, 2026

briefs.about: The Russell 2000 tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies. It shows how smaller businesses, which often depend more on loans and the US economy, are doing.
briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 rose 0.46%, or 12.44 points, on Wednesday to 2,714.31, a small bounce after Tuesday's close of 2,701.87, its lowest in two weeks; it was 2,856.95 on November 4, so smaller companies are still down about 5% since then. It gained on a day when the 10-year rate slipped to about 5.07% and US oil fell 3% to $82.08, while the Dow fell 1.11%. Smaller companies borrow more of their money, often at rates that change, so even a small dip in rates helps their profits, while a Fed hike would hurt them most.

watch.what: Fed decision: a quarter-point hike is expected; a half-point hike would hit small companies hardest, while a softer message could lift them.

briefs.headline: Micron slips to $705.27 even after Nvidia's record quarter
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: Micron is still up about 147% in 2026 but is 41.9% below its June 25 high. Analysts expect sales to more than double to about $278 billion next fiscal year, with $175.61 of profit per share, so the stock costs only about 4 times this year's expected profit. Micron raised its stock buyback plan to $35.2 billion in October, and big buybacks can start December 9 under its government chip-grant rules. Micron also has 26 long-term customer deals covering more than 35% of its expected sales through 2030.
bull: Nvidia's part-buying promises rose to $390 billion from $279 billion, mostly multi-year memory deals, a direct sign of future demand for Micron's chips.
Raymond James expects Micron to spend over $100 billion a year buying back its own stock, which leaves fewer shares and more profit per share.
Micron made $32.9 billion of free cash (money left after costs) in its record quarter, so it can fund new factories and buybacks at once.
bear: Trefis found that after 8 past profit peaks since 2000, Micron's stock was lower a year later every time, by a typical 34.7%.
The stock fell 9.4% in three trading days through November 18 even with Nvidia's strong news, showing investors are nervous about AI spending.
The new November 16 US license rule on AI chip exports to five countries could slow AI chip sales, which would mean less memory needed.
briefs.nextEvent: Micron's next quarterly report, expected in late December 2026

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron closed at $705.27 on November 18, down from $712.42 on November 17 and 9.4% below its $778.31 close on November 13. After Nvidia reported $115.84 billion in quarterly sales on November 17, Micron rose as much as 3.5% before the market opened on November 18, but the gain faded as Nvidia itself slid 2.9% and the selling in AI stocks continued. Almost all of Micron's profit now comes from AI data centers, and Nvidia said its promises to buy parts jumped from $279 billion to $390 billion, mostly long deals for memory, which points to more orders for Micron. The worry is that Micron keeps a record 86.8 cents of gross profit on each sales dollar, and Trefis notes that after past profit peaks the stock was usually lower a year later, because memory prices tend to fall when supply catches up.

watch.what: Micron can start big stock buybacks. Fast buying would show the company thinks its stock is cheap; little buying would be a letdown.
Micron's next quarterly report. Good: a higher sales forecast and steady memory prices. Bad: a lower forecast or signs AI customers are slowing orders.

market.why: On Wednesday, November 18, stocks were mixed: the Dow fell 561 points as health insurer UnitedHealth dropped about 6% on a new government anti-fraud plan, and Nvidia slid 2.9% even after sales jumped 103%. Fed official Christopher Waller said a big half-point rate hike may be needed in December, which worried traders. Tech in the Nasdaq and smaller Russell 2000 companies still edged up as investors got ready for Anthropic's stock debut on Thursday.
